title: 🔥 The Roast: Week 12
preview: The Commish lost the median by fifteen hundredths, Brian fired a running back at 2 AM, Kasik dumped a defense for winning, and Mike benched history. Tap if you can take it.
schedule_note: New roasts drop every Wednesday at 6 PM ET, right after waivers and before Thursday night.
intro: Week 11 gave us a 0.0 from a starting running back, a bench that beat the best team in the league, a commissioner undone by fifteen hundredths of a point, and Brad, somehow, above .500. Week 12 kicks off Thursday. Nobody is safe.
facts_note: Every fact is real: Sleeper Week 11 results and lineups, transactions through Wednesday Nov 25, Week 12 matchups, and AP/NFL game reports. Streaks are head-to-head only. A roast among friends.

entries.roast: Good afternoon, folks, this is your captain speaking. We're currently cruising at eighteen wins, three losses and a tie, and I've gone ahead and turned off the seatbelt sign for the rest of the regular season. Out the right side of the aircraft you'll see Dak Prescott, 41.15 points. Out the left, the other nine teams in this league, very small from up here. Just a little chop to report: our kicker, Shrader, went for 1.0. One point, from a man whose entire job is kicking. Nothing to worry about. This plane basically flies itself. Which is the problem, Jacob. Eighteen wins, and nobody in this league can prove you've touched the controls since September. Sit back, relax, and enjoy the only flight in this league that doesn't end with somebody screaming.
entries.this_week: vs Kyle Llano: 18-3-1 on a two-game win streak, against 10-12 and three straight losses. Kyle's three-game skid is the same number of losses Maddox has all season.
entries.prediction: Maddox wins by 40, and nobody notices the kicker.

entries.roast: Ryan Nussdorfer, come on down! You're the next contestant on The Median Is Right! The median is 134.8. The Commish bids... 134.65. Ohhh. Fifteen hundredths of a point. And folks, he had the winning bid in his hand. Sunday morning he picks up Justice Hill. Hill scores 16.6, with a touchdown, on the bench. Why? Because last week the Commish sat Ryan Flournoy for 19.1, learned his lesson, and started him this week. 2.1. Hill in the flex is 149.15, a clean sweep, and 11-11. Instead the Dictator goes home with the consolation prize: a win over Brian and a long, quiet look at the scoreboard. This man will veto a trade for nine other managers without blinking, and he can't pick one flex.
entries.this_week: vs Nick Cardillo: 10-12 on a one-game win streak, against 6-16 and two straight losses. The Commish draws the Coastal Elites, the closest thing to a bye week anyone's offered him all year.
entries.prediction: Ryan wins by 20 and still finds a flex to regret.

entries.roast: Rachaad, thanks for coming in. Close the door. Have a seat. This isn't easy. Sunday, Brian put you in his starting lineup, and you played 15 snaps. Fifteen. And in those 15 snaps, you touched the ball zero times. Not a carry. Not a target. You scored 0.0 points in a fantasy football game while wearing full pads. Meanwhile Jacory Croskey-Merritt is out on the bench, putting up 15.7 for nobody. Brian had the lowest score in the league, 92.85, and went 0-2. And this is the meeting he chose to have at 1:59 in the morning. Security will walk you out. Don't take it personally, Rachaad. You're not the reason he lost. You're just the only one he could fire without looking in a mirror.
entries.this_week: vs Drew Hartman: 14-8 with a one-game skid, against 11-11 on a one-game win streak. Brian's lead over Kasik for second is one game, and he drew the guy who just remembered how to win.
entries.prediction: Drew wins by 11, and Brian fires somebody before Wednesday's waivers.

entries.roast: We interrupt your regularly scheduled programming with breaking news out of The Implication. Brad Kochheiser is above .500. Officials confirm the last sighting was Week 2. Sources say he dropped 178.7, his second straight week-high, after 213.1 the week before. CeeDee Lamb, 32.2. Mahomes, 29.7. A rookie named Emmett Johnson, 27.3. Kyle Llano was pronounced beaten by 43.75 at the scene. Three straight wins, 11-10-1, and experts are warning this is the most dangerous Brad has ever been, which is to say one game over even. Residents are advised to stay calm. We'll keep you updated, because historically this story has had a very short shelf life.
entries.this_week: vs Nicholas Kasik: 11-10-1 on a three-game win streak, against 13-9 on a three-game win streak. Somebody's streak dies Sunday, and only one of them has been above .500 for longer than a week.
entries.prediction: Kasik wins by 8, and Brad's back to .500 by Monday night.

entries.roast: Welcome to the rose ceremony. Bed, Bath, and Bijan has three straight wins and sits alone in third at 13-9, and tonight, he's handing out roses. Javonte Williams, 24.1 points. Javonte, will you accept this rose? Beautiful. The Chicago Bears defense. 17.35 points. Bears... the Bears are not getting a rose. On waivers, Kasik sent them home for the Giants. By 6:46 this morning, the Giants were gone too, cut for Samaje Perine, with the Jets already moved in. Two breakups before breakfast. Somewhere a defense that just scored 17.35 is crying in the back of the limo, asking what it did wrong. It won, Nick. That's what it did.
entries.this_week: vs Bradley Kochheiser: 13-9 on a three-game win streak, against 11-10-1 on a three-game win streak. Kasik walks in with a defense he met this morning.
entries.prediction: Kasik wins by 8, and the Jets are single again by Wednesday.

entries.roast: Next caller, Kyle, you're on the air. "Yeah, hi, long time listener. Big weekend. Saturday my Wolverines beat number-four UCLA, 18-16, triple overtime. Bowl eligible, baby!" Love it, Kyle. And Sunday? "...Sunday I lost by 43.75." Uh huh. "Jonathan Taylor gave me 6.7." Mm-hm. "And I sat Khalil Shakir's 17.3 on the bench so I could start Rashee Rice for 11.3." Okay. "Three straight losses, 10-12. But hey, I beat the Commish for the median by 0.15!" Kyle, you're calling a sports show to brag about fifteen hundredths of a point. "It counts!" It does, Kyle. Gronk Nation spent Saturday watching a team that refused to lose and Sunday being one. We'll take a quick break.
entries.this_week: vs Jacob Maddox: 10-12 and three straight losses, against 18-3-1 on a two-game win streak. Kyle needs a miracle, and he spent his on Saturday.
entries.prediction: Maddox wins by 40, and Kyle calls back in to talk about basketball season.

entries.roast: CARDILLO! Come here. What is this? "It's Michael Mayer, Chef." When did he come in? "Wednesday, Chef." And you served him Sunday? "Yes, Chef." 1.4 POINTS! It's RAW! And what's this next to it? "Monangai, Chef. 1.8." And this? "Luther Burden, Chef. 3.3." Three starters, 6.5 points between them, on the same plate! Kasik beat you by 31, you're 6-16, two straight losses, and the only thing you cooked all week was your own season. You named the restaurant the Coastal Elites, Nick. People with taste. Look at this plate. Shut it down.
entries.this_week: vs Ryan Nussdorfer: 6-16 and two straight losses, against 10-12 on a one-game win streak. Cardillo has four games left to make 6-16 look like a choice.
entries.prediction: Ryan wins by 20, and Cardillo sends out another tight end raw.

entries.roast: "Hi. My name is Drew, and I'm .500." (Hi, Drew.) "Six games in, I was 0-6. Rock bottom. But I took it one week at a time. Sunday, Chuba Hubbard gave me 29.0. DJ Moore gave me 23.1. I beat Mike by 17.55, I'm 11-11, and I'm 11-5 since rock bottom." (Applause.) "I just want to thank my sponsor, the waiver wire, and my higher power, the median." Drew, that's beautiful. Jordan Belfort's Nuts are clean and sober at exactly .500. For a team named after a guy who went to federal prison, that's one hell of a recovery. Keep coming back, buddy. It works if you work it, and if Hubbard doesn't.
entries.this_week: vs Brian Mulvihill: 11-11 on a one-game win streak, against 14-8 with a one-game skid. One more win and Drew has to learn what a winning record feels like.
entries.prediction: Drew wins by 11, and the support group loses its best success story.

entries.roast: JUST LISTED: Charming 4-18 fixer-upper in East Lansing! Six straight losses and priced to move. Features a fully stocked bench: Ashton Jeanty, 29.9 points, and Ladd McConkey, 19.7, both healthy, both untouched. Seller instead staged the living room with Cam Skattebo (4.8, includes one lost fumble) and Adonai Mitchell (5.0). Swap those two and this property scores 170.8, more than Maddox's 169.25. Owner lost to the best team in the league with the winning lineup in the basement. Recently updated defense: Ravens out, Commanders in this morning. Quarterback room renovated today: Aaron Rodgers removed, Mason Rudolph installed. Neighborhood just lost 45-7 on Senior Day. Motivated seller. Extremely motivated.
entries.this_week: vs Mike Hemstreet: 4-18 and six straight losses, against 12-10 with a one-game skid. Taylor's about to get pulled over by the league cop with a Mason Rudolph he picked up this morning and no good explanation.
entries.prediction: Mike wins by 30, and Taylor relists the defense Wednesday.

entries.roast: Sunday, November 22nd, 2026. Travis Kelce catches two touchdowns against Arizona, and with them, passes Rob Gronkowski on the all-time tight end touchdown list. 25.4 fantasy points. A moment for the history books. And in the history books of MagicSkolBussss, the entry for that afternoon reads, simply: "Bench." Mike started T.J. Hockenson instead. 11.5. Now, historians will note that even with Kelce, Mike still loses to Drew by 3.65. That's the real tragedy, Mike. You couldn't even blame it on him. Two losses, 12-10, Kasik slides past him into third, and today he cut the Lions defense he picked up a week ago for Brandon Aiyuk. Future generations will ask where they were when Kelce passed Gronk. Mike was staring right at him, on his own bench.
entries.this_week: vs Taylor Alvarado: 12-10 with a one-game skid, against 4-18 and six straight losses. Mike's cure for a two-game skid is a man on a six-game one.
entries.prediction: Mike wins by 30 and leaves something historic on the bench.
